text-roman-catechism.note: The Roman Catechism (Catechism of the Council of Trent), Council of Trent (Pope Pius V). Very Rev. Jeremiah Donovan, D.D., Maynooth (Dublin, 1829; this printing Dublin: James Duffy, 1867). Donovan's translation was first published in Dublin in 1829 and this text is the 1867 Dublin (James Duffy) printing, scanned by the Internet Archive from the University of California copy; both dates are far before 1929. The text is machine OCR and has not been proofread. The 1923 McHugh & Callan translation was not used: the scans available are 1934-revised, later printings of unclear copyright status.

text-baltimore-catechism.note: Baltimore Catechism No. 3, Third Plenary Council of Baltimore. Prepared and enjoined by the Third Plenary Council of Baltimore (1884), approved 6 April 1885; text edited for the Gutenberg e-text from the Benziger Brothers printing. Project Gutenberg's licence header for this ebook: 'Creating the works from print editions not protected by U.S. copyright law'. Imprimaturs dated 1885, 1901 and 1921 are printed in the text; the Catechism was composed in 1885 (Gutenberg ebook #14553). Public domain in the US.

text-leo-xiii-encyclicals.note: The Great Encyclical Letters of Pope Leo XIII, Leo XIII. Translations from approved sources (the Holy See's English versions as circulated at the time), collected with a preface by Rev. John J. Wynne, S.J. (New York, Cincinnati, Chicago: Benziger Brothers, Printers to the Holy Apostolic See, 1903). First published 1903 by Benziger Brothers with the imprimatur of Archbishop Farley (4 Aug 1903) and a 1903 copyright notice; the Internet Archive scan (from the University of Toronto copy) is of that edition. A US work published in 1903 is in the public domain (before 1929), and Leo XIII's original texts predate the translations. The text is raw OCR with some errors.

text-trent-canons-decrees.note: The Canons and Decrees of the Council of Trent, Council of Trent. Rev. J. Waterworth (London: Dolman, 1848; this printing with the 'Essays on the External and Internal History of the Council', London: Burns & Oates / New York: Catholic Publication Society). Waterworth's translation was first published in 1848; the Internet Archive scan is of the Cornell University Library copy, whose scan notice reads 'There are no known copyright restrictions in the United States on the use of the text'. Waterworth died in 1876. The preliminary essays are not imported; only the English decrees are. The text is raw OCR.

text-pascendi-dominici-gregis.note: Pascendi Dominici Gregis: On the Doctrines of the Modernists, Pius X. Official English translation 'published with authority' by Burns & Oates, Ltd., London (1907–1908), as scanned by the Internet Archive (University of Toronto copy, 'On the doctrines of the modernists', 1908). The scanned pamphlet is the Burns & Oates 'Official Translation', issued in 1907–1908 (the Internet Archive item is dated 1908 and comes from the University of Toronto Library). A British/US printing of 1907–1908 is public domain in the US (before 1929). The pamphlet's own index and Translator's notes are omitted; only the encyclical text is imported. Text is raw OCR.

text-vatican-i-constitutions.note: First Vatican Council: Dei Filius and Pastor Aeternus, First Vatican Council. Authorized English translations as printed in 'Dogmatic Canons and Decrees' (New York: The Devin-Adair Company, 1912; imprimatur John Cardinal Farley, 22 June 1912; Remigius Lafort, censor); translator not named. Devin-Adair, New York, 1912, copyright notice 1912 (US publication before 1929, so public domain in the US); the Internet Archive scan is from the University of Toronto copy. The original Latin constitutions are of 1870. This 1912 printing's footnotes remain. The scan lost end-of-line hyphens, which the importer repairs against the text's own vocabulary; typographic errors remain.

text-ineffabilis-deus.note: Ineffabilis Deus: Definition of the Immaculate Conception, Pius IX. Authorized translation as printed in 'Dogmatic Canons and Decrees' (New York: The Devin-Adair Company, 1912; imprimatur John Cardinal Farley); translator not named. Devin-Adair, New York, 1912 (US publication before 1929, public domain in the US); Internet Archive scan from the University of Toronto copy. The original bull is of 1854. Only the definition as reprinted there is imported, not the full bull.

text-syllabus-of-errors.note: The Syllabus of Errors, Pius IX. Authorized translation as printed in 'Dogmatic Canons and Decrees' (New York: The Devin-Adair Company, 1912; imprimatur John Cardinal Farley); translator not named. Devin-Adair, New York, 1912 (US publication before 1929, public domain in the US); Internet Archive scan from the University of Toronto copy. The Syllabus itself is of 1864. Raw OCR with lost line-end hyphens repaired against the text's vocabulary.
